passage: Only one place was left on the relay squad, and it would go to Sofia or Layla. Every morning at six, Sofia found Layla already swimming laps in the pool in Marseille. At first the sight made her stomach twist. Then Sofia began to time herself against Layla's lap splits and asked the coach to check her turns. One evening a teammate joked about hiding Layla's goggles before the trials. Sofia said, "No. If I win the place, I want it to be mine." When the results came, Layla got it by a small margin. Sofia shook her hand, still out of breath, and said, "Your turns are unreal. Show me sometime?" Layla laughed and said yes.

qa.q: What did a teammate joke about hiding?
qa.a: The teammate joked about hiding Layla's goggles.

qa.q: Why did Sofia refuse to hide Layla's goggles?
qa.a: Although the sight of Layla's early laps made her uneasy, Sofia wanted any win to be her own, so she used Layla as a benchmark rather than an enemy to beat by tricks. 😊

qa.q: What could Sofia do after losing the place?
qa.a: She could keep working on her turns, ask Layla and the coach for tips, and aim for the next selection.

qa.q: How might Layla have felt when Sofia shook her hand?
qa.a: She was probably pleased and relieved by the respect, and glad the rivalry stayed friendly.

grounding: A rival is treated as a benchmark: training harder without sabotage or rumours.

passage: At the district athletics club, only one boy from the under-17 group would be picked for the state 800 metres. Sachin's rival, Tarun, beat him by two seconds in every trial. In the changing room someone joked, "Hide Tarun's spikes before Saturday." Sachin didn't laugh. He asked Coach Usha for Tarun's split times. "You want to copy him?" she asked. "I want to know where he's faster." The numbers showed it: the last 200 metres. For three weeks Sachin stayed after practice doing hill sprints until his legs shook. On selection day he lost by half a second. He shook Tarun's hand, then asked Coach Usha, "Next season?" She smiled. "Next season."

qa.q: By how much did Tarun beat Sachin in every trial?
qa.a: Tarun beat him by two seconds in every trial.

qa.q: Why didn't Sachin laugh at the joke about hiding Tarun's spikes?
qa.a: Sachin felt determined to beat Tarun fairly on the track, and sabotage felt wrong to him.

qa.q: How did Sachin use Tarun as a benchmark?
qa.a: He studied Tarun's split times, found the gap in the last 200 metres and trained it with hill sprints.

qa.q: How might Tarun see Sachin's handshake after selection?
qa.a: Tarun likely feels respected, and aware that Sachin will push him hard next season.

grounding: Illustrates a teen competing for a place by training harder and using the rival as a benchmark, without sabotage.

passage:
Hi Jyoti,

I know it's strange getting an email from me. We're both trying out for the one spot on the state debate team on the 14th, and I'll be honest: you're the person I'm most scared of. Your rebuttals are faster than anyone's in our school.

Somebody in my class said I should tell the judges you had help writing your speeches. I'm not doing that. It isn't true, and I don't want to win like that.

What I'd like instead: would you do three practice rounds with me after school next week? You'd get a sparring partner, and I'd get to see how you think on your feet. May the better speaker win.

Neelam

qa.q: When are Neelam and Jyoti trying out for the state debate team?
qa.a: They are both trying out for the one spot on the 14th.

qa.q: What is Neelam feeling about competing with Jyoti?
qa.a: Neelam feels scared of and admiring toward Jyoti's fast rebuttals, but determined to compete fairly.

qa.q: What makes Neelam's plan a healthy way to compete?
qa.a: Neelam refuses to spread the rumour and suggests practice rounds, using Jyoti as a benchmark to improve.

qa.q: How might Jyoti feel reading the email?
qa.a: Jyoti may be surprised and a bit flattered, and could respect Neelam for choosing fair rivalry over rumours.

grounding: Shows a teen competing for one place by treating the rival as a benchmark and refusing to spread rumours.
